dimensions.rationale: The title and KPI values are identifiable, but the oversized header void, detached navigation, repetitive KPI morphology, and nested insight panel weaken the analytical scan path.
Six large KPI tiles expose only labels and totals, while the insight panel and modals use more surface area than their information warrants.
Core controls are recognizable, but resting range actions look ambiguously unavailable and the export selector lacks a compact selection summary.
Active navigation, export selections, overlays, and fallback mode are visible, but inactive controls are subdued and fallback values are inconsistently formatted.
The grids align, but competing header anchors and a drilldown with crowded plotting and equally weighted hourly signals reduce coherence.
Muted labels, descriptions, chart ticks, and navigation text are small and low contrast, while some states depend heavily on subtle color differences.
The shell and palette preserve FitTrack branding, but analytics morphology remains close to a generic dark SaaS dashboard.

findings.observation: The title, right-aligned section navigation, date panel, and attendance action occupy separate visual axes.
findings.user_impact: Admins must reconstruct the reading order and the first viewport feels stretched.
findings.repair_direction: Collapse the header gap and associate controls and section actions with their content.
findings.verification: Full and compact views have one dominant title followed by one coherent scope-and-control band.

findings.observation: Six equal KPI cards give total revenue, contributing revenue streams, and operational counts identical weight without supported comparison context.
findings.user_impact: The dashboard reports values without distinguishing headline outcome, contributors, and operational drivers.
findings.repair_direction: Create explicit metric grouping and reduce repetitive card anatomy without inventing unsupported trends.
findings.verification: A first-glance scan distinguishes headline revenue, revenue contributors, and operational drivers.

findings.observation: Small muted labels recur across the route and raw fallback numbers do not match surrounding currency formatting.
findings.user_impact: Scanning takes more effort and fallback presentation appears unfinished.
findings.repair_direction: Raise local secondary readability and format fallback values consistently.
findings.verification: Supporting copy is readable and all fallback metric values use recognizable localized formatting.

findings.observation: The export selection and tied peak-hour signals use repeated equal-weight treatments rather than task-focused summaries.
findings.user_impact: Selection and drilldown tasks require more visual parsing than necessary.
findings.repair_direction: Add a compact export selection summary and explicitly communicate tied peak-hour results.
findings.verification: The export selection count and drilldown tie state are immediately understandable.

dimensions.rationale: The page and modal titles establish a usable path, but the masthead gap, detached tabs, and dominant fallback panel weaken prioritization.
Large KPI and export tiles expose little decision context, while the drilldown provides limited interpretive depth.
Primary actions and selections are recognizable, but the export flow lacks a selected-count summary and resting range controls need clearer state context.
Active and fallback states are identified, but technical fallback status competes with the result and identical peak values are not explained as a tie.
The KPI grid, responsive range panel, and modals are structurally coherent, though the masthead and repeated containers remain spatially loose.
Descriptions, timestamps, section labels, disabled controls, and chart ticks are visually small or low contrast against dark surfaces.
The palette and gym terminology are consistent, but generic card morphology and exposed provider diagnostics weaken product confidence.

findings.observation: The main insight prominently exposes provider unavailability and unformatted deterministic fallback values.
findings.user_impact: Implementation status appears before business meaning and reduces trust.
findings.repair_direction: Demote provider status, keep the business readout primary, and format all values consistently.
findings.verification: Business meaning dominates while provider status is secondary and monetary values are localized.

findings.observation: KPI cards contain only labels and values despite the selected six-month range.
findings.user_impact: Admins cannot distinguish headline outcomes from contributors and operational drivers.
findings.repair_direction: Add honest grouping and reduce footprint where comparison data is unavailable.
findings.verification: KPI grouping communicates the metric relationship without invented trend data.

findings.observation: Supporting copy, timestamps, export descriptions, and chart ticks use subdued gray and small typography.
findings.user_impact: Frequent admin scanning becomes slower and state recognition is less certain.
findings.repair_direction: Raise local secondary contrast and minimum sizes while preserving hierarchy.
findings.verification: Supporting content and control states remain immediately readable at both viewport sizes.

findings.observation: Five peak-hour signals share the same value but the interface does not explain that no single peak exists.
findings.user_impact: The modal appears detailed without yielding an unambiguous attendance conclusion.
findings.repair_direction: State the tie explicitly and present the shared peak window compactly.
findings.verification: The modal communicates a tied peak state without requiring inference.
